summary:
The Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2024, provides full-year appropriations for fiscal year 2024 across six major divisions (Defense, Financial Services and General Government, Homeland Security, Labor/Health and Human Services/Education, Legislative Branch, and State/Foreign Operations) and includes a seventh division for other matters. It also enacts numerous policy riders and conditions on the use of funds. The Act designates that the House Appropriations Chair’s explanatory statement printed in the Congressional Record around March 22, 2024, serves as the official allocation and implementation guide for Divisions A through F. It further prohibits any cost-of-living pay adjustment for Members of Congress during FY2024.

Division A, the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, appropriates substantial sums for military personnel, including $50.04 billion for the Army, $36.71 billion for the Navy, $15.27 billion for the Marine Corps, $36.20 billion for the Air Force, and $1.26 billion for the Space Force, along with funding for reserve and National Guard components. Operation and Maintenance funding totals $58.60 billion for the Army, $71.97 billion for the Navy, $10.18 billion for the Marine Corps, $61.47 billion for the Air Force, $4.90 billion for the Space Force, and $52.60 billion for Defense-Wide activities. The Act imposes numerous conditions, including a prohibition on transferring armor-piercing ammunition to non-governmental entities except for demilitarization or authorized manufacturing, a requirement for 15-day advance reporting to defense committees on new defense innovation acceleration projects exceeding $5 million, and a mandate that the National Intelligence Program’s budget structure not be modified without joint certification from the Director of National Intelligence and the Secretary of Defense. It also provides $100 million for cooperation and interoperability efforts with African and Southern Commands, subject to advance execution plans and notifications.

Division B covers Financial Services and General Government. It appropriates $78.90 million for White House salaries and expenses, $15.45 million for the Executive Residence, $114.31 million for the Office of Administration, and $129.00 million for the Office of Management and Budget. The Office of National Drug Control Policy’s High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas program receives $298.58 million, with at least 51 percent required to be transferred to state and local entities within 120 days of enactment. The division also authorizes the return of certain Social Security Act funds to the Treasury’s Cybersecurity Enhancement Account.

Division D, covering the Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, contains several notable policy changes. It authorizes Indian tribes operating Head Start programs to establish their own selection criteria, overriding standard income eligibility requirements, and allows migrant and seasonal Head Start programs to do the same, giving priority to children of migrant farmworker families. The Act creates a two-year exemption from Fair Labor Standards Act overtime requirements for disaster claims adjusters following a declared disaster. It rescinds $1.25 billion in unobligated balances from the Nonrecurring Expenses Fund by September 30, 2024, and rescinds an additional $70 million from prior HHS Children and Families Services appropriations for incentive payment grants to states.

Division F, the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, imposes detailed conditions on foreign assistance. It prohibits direct funding to governments of Independent States of the former Soviet Union that violate the territorial integrity of another state, subject to a presidential national security waiver. Assistance to Ukraine is conditioned on a 50 percent cost-matching requirement, limiting U.S. contributions to half of total assistance from all sources; the President may waive this requirement in the national security interest and must report every 120 days on efforts to increase other donor contributions. The Act mandates a comprehensive Ukraine strategy within 60 days, in-person monitoring of project-based assistance, and joint certification that oversight mechanisms are in place before obligating funds. It also requires detailed quarterly reports on all Ukraine assistance, which must be made publicly available. Funds are prohibited from supporting defense article sales to the Turkish Presidential Protection Directorate unless indicted members return to the United States for trial, with exceptions for border security and NATO operations.
